pr.title: feat(accounts): resolve or provision OIDC users
pr.author: gilmishal
pr.head: 4142977c6

lead.heading: What the change accomplishes
lead.text: PR #2224 adds `POST /api/v1/accounts/internal/users/resolve-or-provision` to the accounts service: given an OIDC identity (`issuer`, `subject`) and the claims web-bff forwards from the token (`preferred_username`, `name`, `email`, `avatar_url`), it returns the existing user for that identity or creates one, so a first login provisions an account with no separate registration step. The route is guarded by an internal API key (`FLOXHUB_ACCOUNTS_INTERNAL_API_KEYS`, a comma-separated set so keys can rotate) rather than by an end-user token, and it is mounted in every authentication mode, SaaS included.

lead.heading: The mechanism it rests on
lead.text: `user_service.py` looks the identity up by `(issuer, subject)`. On a miss it derives the user id as `uuid5(NAMESPACE_URL, issuer + NUL + subject)`, derives a handle from `preferred_username` (falling back to `name`) through the same normalization web-bff's `sanitizeToHandleShape` applies, writes the user, identity, and handle rows in one transaction, and then writes the two FGA ownership tuples. A unique-constraint failure on that insert is read as a concurrent first login and resolved to whichever request won, a handle already taken answers 409, and a login that finds the user stamps `last_login_at` and reasserts the FGA grants, so a grant lost to an FGA failure after the commit is repaired by the next login.

verdict: The code does what the description says on every path I could execute, including the two paths the PR's own tests don't reach (the insert race and an FGA failure after commit). The defects are at the contract and prose layer: one unhandled exception on unauthenticated input, a scheme match that disagrees with the sibling parser, an OpenAPI contract that still advertises the 404 Nick asked to drop and omits the 201 the code returns, and three written claims the artifact contradicts.
limit_line: Nothing here exercised a real OpenFGA store, Postgres under two genuinely concurrent transactions (the race probe forces a lookup miss rather than racing), uvicorn's header parsing (the non-ASCII probe ran through Starlette's TestClient), or deployed routing on either environment.
risk_pointer: Low to medium: the change adds an internal endpoint behind the internal API key and alters nothing that exists, but what it stores persists — the uuid5-derived user id and the claimed handle — so a wrong derivation would need a data fix rather than a redeploy; that derivation is now test-pinned.

sections.title: Correctness
sections.blurb: What I could verify by running or reading. `Did not hold` is what the reader acts on; `Held` is the evidence behind the verdict.

items.summary: A non-ASCII bearer raises `TypeError` out of `hmac.compare_digest` — a 500 for unauthenticated callers
items.detail: A latin-1 `Authorization: Bearer café` reaches `hmac.compare_digest` at `dependencies.py:211` and raises `TypeError: comparing strings with non-ASCII characters is not supported`. Unauthenticated callers get a 500 instead of a 401. Fix: compare `.encode()`d bytes, or pre-check ASCII.

items.summary: The `Bearer` scheme match is case-sensitive, unlike the sibling parser in the same process and the `WWW-Authenticate` it emits
items.detail: `dependencies.py:197` matches the scheme with `startswith('Bearer ')`. The public routes in the same process authenticate through FastAPI's `HTTPBearer` (`catalog_common/auth/auth0_strategy.py:71`), which matches with `scheme.lower() != 'bearer'`, and the 401 sets `WWW-Authenticate: Bearer`, invoking RFC 6750, whose scheme token is case-insensitive per RFC 7235 §2.1. So `bearer <token>` is accepted on `/tokens` and rejected on `/internal/users/…`. `test_p2_config_edge_cases` confirms `bearer k1` → 401. The one live caller (web-bff) sends `Bearer`, so nothing breaks today.

items.summary: OpenAPI still advertises 404 on `resolve-or-provision`, omits the 201 the code returns, and lists 409/503 on `get-by-id`
items.detail: Reading `/openapi.json`: `resolve-or-provision` advertises `200/401/404/409/422/503` and no `201`; `get-by-id` advertises `409/503` it cannot produce. Cause: `users.py:52` shares one `_ERRORS` dict across both routes, and the POST declares no 201. The review-thread fix (70fec72d1) removed the 404 code path but not the advertised response. web-bff (#2187) checks `response.ok`, so the client tolerates the 201.

items.summary: `claude.md` says claims arrive from an 'OIDC token endpoint gate' that was closed unmerged
items.detail: `src/accounts/.claude/claude.md:31` — 'receives claims only after the OIDC token endpoint gate has verified them.' That gate is PR #2221, closed unmerged on 2026-08-17 as 'no longer part of the stack'; the live design verifies in web-bff's callback (#2187). Stale the moment it merges.

items.summary: README says the internal routes are 'not exposed through the public Accounts route' — false on SaaS by design
items.detail: `src/accounts/README.md:154` — 'not exposed through the public Accounts route.' On SaaS, API Gateway routes `ANY /accounts/{proxy+}` (`terraform/units/accounts/api_gateway.tf:17`) and web-bff hairpins through `https://api.*.flox.dev/accounts` (`terraform/units/web-bff/ecs.tf:172`), which is what ENT-225 means by 'the key is the only thing standing in front.' On-prem it becomes true only when #2187 adds `location /accounts/api/v1/accounts/internal/ { return 404; }`.

items.summary: The `email` column comment says 'refreshed at login'; the code never refreshes
items.detail: `models.py:96` (from PR #2105) says `email` is 'seeded at provisioning, refreshed at login'. `test_p9_second_login_stamps_only_last_login` — a second login carrying a new email and avatar leaves both untouched and bumps only `last_login_at`. The code conforms to ENT-191 ('nothing reads provider claims after creation'); the comment, and the design doc §5.1 it descends from, say the opposite. Which side is stale is B1.

items.evidence: mutation: delete the regrant at user_service.py:108, then just accounts test -k test_users
items.summary: No test binds the FGA regrant in the insert-race recovery branch (`user_service.py:108`)
items.detail: Deleting the regrant in the race branch (`user_service.py:108`) leaves all 8 PR tests green. `test_p3_race_recovers_existing_user` (monkeypatches `UserRepository.find_identity` to miss once, so the insert hits the `handles` primary key and the `IntegrityError` branch runs) is the only thing that catches the deletion.

items.evidence: ENT-191 'Report back on' vs the PR body
items.summary: ENT-191's three 'report back on' items are unanswered in the PR body
items.detail: How a caller supplies its own handle: no path exists — `LoginInput` has no `handle`. The wire shape of the operator-visible failure: `422 {'detail': 'Invalid handle: <length|format|unavailable>'}`, `409 {'detail': 'Handle is unavailable'}`, `422 {'detail': 'OIDC identity has no preferred_username or name claim'}`. Whether it landed behind ENT-225: yes — this PR carries its own `require_internal_api_key`; #2226 wired the terraform ahead of it.

items.evidence: CI run 32853773279 on 4142977c6; just accounts test in the audit worktree
items.summary: CI is green on the head SHA and the suite passes locally (117 tests)
items.detail: CI run 32853773279 on head `4142977c6`: accounts dev-env ×2, Nix build ×2, NEF, pre-commit, every integration matrix. `just accounts test` in `~/src/floxhub-worktrees/audit-pr2224-resolve-or-provision` → 117 passed. The probe file is `src/accounts/tests/test_audit_probes.py` there, untracked; `just accounts test -k test_p` runs it.

items.summary: An FGA failure after the DB commit leaves the user row, and a retry writes the grants
items.detail: `FakeFga.write` raises after the database commit; the user row is present, FGA is empty, and a second POST returns 200 with both ownership tuples. Repair-by-retry holds as claimed.

items.summary: The insert race resolves to the winner's user with grants reasserted
items.detail: Monkeypatches `UserRepository.find_identity` to miss once, so the insert hits the `handles` primary key and the `IntegrityError` branch runs. Returns 200 with the winner's id and both tuples regranted.

items.summary: Empty and whitespace-only key configuration refuses every bearer; a rotation set accepts each member
items.detail: Configurations `''`, `' , '`, `','` refuse every bearer including the empty one; `'k1, k2 ,'` accepts `k1` and `k2` and rejects `k1 `. Fail-closed holds. The PR's own `test_internal_user_routes_fail_closed` covers missing and wrong keys only, not empty configuration.

items.evidence: node vs python3 over 15 inputs; test_p7_normalization
items.summary: Handle normalization is byte-identical to web-bff's `sanitizeToHandleShape`
items.detail: 15 edge inputs through web-bff's `sanitizeToHandleShape` under node and the Python port are byte-identical (`Zoë Müller → zo-m-ller`, `ß → ''`, `ﬁsh → sh`, `İstanbul → i-stanbul`). `test_p7_normalization` adds eight parametrized cases including `FIRST_LAST → first-last`, `flox-admin → 422 unavailable`, a UUID → 422 unavailable, `--- → 422 length`.

items.summary: A handle collision leaves no identity, user, or handle row behind
items.detail: After the 409, exactly one row in each of `identities`, `users`, `handles`; the losing identity is not linked.

items.evidence: mutations: delete the regrant in _record_login; change the uuid5 separator
items.summary: The PR's tests bind the login-time regrant and the exact uuid5 derivation
items.detail: Deleting the regrant in `_record_login` fails `test_provisioning_is_idempotent_by_issuer_and_subject`; changing the uuid5 separator from `\0` to `/` fails `test_first_login_derives_handle_id_and_personal_ownership`. Both bind.

items.evidence: ENT-191 Must / Must not vs the diff
items.summary: Ticket coverage: every Must and Must-not that belongs to accounts is met
items.detail: Must 1/2/3/5 met; Must 4 and Must-not 1 belong to web-bff (#2187); Must-not 2 met (the idempotency test plus A11); Must-not 3 met, derivation lives in accounts.

items.summary: The wire contract with #2187 matches end to end
items.detail: Path `/api/v1/accounts/internal/users/resolve-or-provision`, body `identity.{issuer,subject}` / `preferred_username` / `name` / `email` / `avatar_url`, `Authorization: Bearer`, env var `FLOXHUB_ACCOUNTS_INTERNAL_API_KEYS` (terraform from #2226 and the dev shell already export it).

sections.title: Decisions the PR made that only you can judge
sections.blurb: Each item names a choice the author already encoded, what it turns on, where that is grounded, and what stays if you say nothing. Ordered by what reading the PR will not reveal, durable before local — never by significance.

groups.title: Lead — the ones I'd push back on

items.summary: `models.py:96` says `email` is 'refreshed at login'; the code seeds it once and never refreshes it — which of the two is stale?
items.turns_on: Whether ENT-191's 'syncing profile data on later logins is additive and out' means rejected (rewrite the comment to match the code) or deferred (leave the comment as the intended end state and accept that the code is behind it for now).
items.grounded: ENT-191 for the behavior; design doc §5.1 and the comment for the end state.
items.default: The comment stays as written and the code stays behind it.

items.summary: One `resolve-or-provision` with derivation inside accounts replaces the design doc's two calls — and drops the caller-supplied handle
items.turns_on: Whether the Auth0 Action (ENT-236) or any interactive picker can live without a caller-supplied `handle`.
items.grounded: ENT-191 Must-not #3 for moving derivation in; nothing for dropping the supplied-handle half of design doc §5.1 (`POST /internal/logins` plus `POST /users`).

items.summary: Stored format: `users.id = uuid5(NAMESPACE_URL, f'{issuer}\0{subject}')`, now CI-pinned
items.turns_on: Whether an edge will ever derive `user:{id}` without a lookup, and whether a Dex connector rename (which changes subjects) should change the id.
items.grounded: Review thread ('leaves that possibility open'); ENT-224 said 'accounts-minted UUID'; design doc §3.1 argues subjects are unstable on-prem. `test_first_login_derives_handle_id_and_personal_ownership` pins the exact derivation.

items.summary: Two id schemes in one `users` table: rows this endpoint creates get a deterministic uuid5 of issuer and subject; rows any other writer creates keep the random `uuid4` default
items.turns_on: Whether a row's id must be derivable from its first identity for every user, or only for OIDC-provisioned ones. The other writers are the Auth0-Action registration path (ENT-236) and any import; if an edge ever derives `user:{id}` from the token (B3), users those writers created would be unreachable that way.
items.grounded: `models.py:75` records the split ('other writers retain the random default'); nothing found that says whether ENT-236 should derive ids the same way.

items.summary: An FGA write on every login, not only on retry after a failure
items.turns_on: FGA write cost per login versus repair-only-on-retry.
items.grounded: ENT-227 said 'repaired by retrying the call or by the reconciler'; the PR's `claude.md` text reframes it as 'reasserted when provisioned again'.

items.summary: On-prem key configuration lives in #2187; this PR alone leaves every on-prem internal call at 401
items.turns_on: Stack order only.
items.grounded: #2187's diff sets `FLOXHUB_ACCOUNTS_INTERNAL_API_KEYS` from the on-prem secrets dir.

items.summary: `issuer`/`subject` are bare `str`; an empty pair provisions a user
items.turns_on: Callers always having verified the token before calling.
items.grounded: Nothing in accounts. `test_p10_empty_identity_pair` — `''`/`''` → 201.

items.summary: `preferred_username or name`: an empty-string `preferred_username` falls through to `name`
items.turns_on: Whether Dex ever emits `''` for a present claim.
items.grounded: ENT-191 Must #2 says 'absent'. `test_p7_normalization` case `'' / 'Fallback Name' → fallback-name`.

items.summary: Non-ASCII usernames become hyphen-garbled handles; a name that normalizes to `''`, `flox*`, or a UUID shape is a 422 with no picker
items.turns_on: Whether the operator-visible failure is the right outcome for those directory users.
items.grounded: ENT-191 Must #3 and 'You may assume #2'.

items.summary: When the provisioning insert fails on a unique constraint and no identity row exists for the pair afterward, the service answers 409 'Handle is unavailable' — it assumes the handle was the constraint that fired
items.turns_on: The handle, `users.id`, and the `(issuer, subject)` pair being the only unique constraints across the three tables. A constraint added later (a unique `email`, say) would surface as a misleading 409 rather than its own error.
items.grounded: Schema in `models.py` — `email` is not unique, and `users.id` is a function of the identity pair, so a collision on it implies the pair was already linked. Sound today.

items.summary: Status mapping: `HandleUnavailable`→409, `InvalidLogin`→422, anything else re-raised as 500
items.turns_on: What web-bff and an operator do with each.
items.grounded: ENT-227 for 409; nothing for 422 over 400.

items.summary: Error bodies carry the rejection reason and never the handle or username
items.turns_on: The Sentry-PII posture for handles.
items.grounded: Consistent with the contested posture (AI-178).

items.summary: `signup_completed_at` and `onboarding_completed_at` both set at provisioning
items.turns_on: Whether on-prem has an onboarding step to gate.
items.grounded: web-bff's on-prem services already hardcode both true (`PosixUserService.ts:49`, `AccountsUserService.ts:22`).

items.summary: `display_name = name`, so with `preferred_username` absent, `name` seeds both handle and display name
items.turns_on: What display name a username-only identity should carry.
items.grounded: Nothing beyond the ticket naming `name` as the username fallback.

items.summary: The internal router is mounted in every `authn_mode`, SaaS `auth0` included
items.turns_on: SaaS exposure behind the key being acceptable.
items.grounded: ENT-225 outcome ('reachable from the internet, the key is the only thing in front').

items.summary: ENT-225 Must #2 — `GET /internal/users/{id}` carries the end-user principal only as a path param, not in the shared assertion header
items.turns_on: Whether the assertion-header rule applies to a lookup made while constructing the session.
items.grounded: ENT-225; nothing in the PR addresses it.

items.summary: `internal_api_keys: str = ''`, comma-separated, whitespace stripped
items.turns_on: The SSM value shape.
items.grounded: ENT-225 Must #1; terraform `/floxhub/{env}/accounts/internal-api-keys`.

items.summary: A `session.flush()` sits between adding the user and adding the identity (`user_service.py:97`); deleting it changes nothing
items.turns_on: Nothing today: the `Identity.user` relationship makes SQLAlchemy order the user insert before the identity insert on its own. With the flush deleted, all 8 PR tests and the audit probes pass.
items.grounded: Mutation run (`just accounts test -k test_users`, then `-k test_p`, with the line removed).

items.summary: The PR adds a one-way `Identity.user` relationship (`models.py:141`) and no `User.identities` collection, so a user's identities are reachable only by query
items.turns_on: Whether a consumer will need to walk user → identities. The reconciler snapshot in design doc §5.8 exports each user with `identities: [{issuer, subject}]`, which is that walk, and ENT-231 builds it. A consumer that needs it either queries `identities` by `user_id` or adds `User.identities`; adding that side later without `back_populates` leaves the two sides unsynchronized within a session (an identity appended to `user.identities` does not set `identity.user` until flush and reload), which is the case a two-sided declaration exists to prevent.
items.grounded: The relationship was added at review, so the type system shows the user must exist (Nick's comment on 8faf18306; fixed in 70fec72d1). Design doc §5.8 for the coming user → identities walk.
items.default: One-way stays; a consumer needing the reverse walk queries `identities` by `user_id`.

items.summary: The race-branch regrant has no test in the PR
items.turns_on: Whether the audit probe (or a two-transaction version) should be kept.
